_how: Football team names, for reading handwritten betting slips: what a customer writes, which team that is, and how Betty's shop feed names it.
Added to, never guessed: a written name that isn't here isn't understood. A written name under two teams needs the user's ruling (check_team_names.py lists any without one).
'name' is the club's full name. 'shorthand' is what a UK punter writes, compared without capitals, accents, full stops or apostrophes.
'former' is a name the club used to have. 'league' is this season's, as of 'checked'. 'europe' is its UEFA league phase this season, if any. 'note' is a warning for whoever reads the entry.

'till' is every name the shop feed has for the team, copied exactly from the results of its Match Betting market (the BFB files) or its Full Time Result market (the league files, such as Germ2). They can differ: 'Arminia Bielefeld' and 'A Bielefeld'.

An empty 'till' means no match of theirs was in the feed when checked, not that Betty doesn't know them. Feed names over 24 characters are cut in the middle ('Us Orleans L.Et Football'), and event names are cut short ('Sparta Pra V Bournemout').

'rulings' says what a written name under two teams means on its own: one team's full name, or 'use opponent' (never accepted alone: the opponent on the slip has to settle it, or it isn't guessed). The name stays listed under all its teams. The user accepted these on 5 Nov 2026 as suggested: they're judgement calls, not researched facts, and can be changed here.

'unsure' is what couldn't be supported: nothing there counts as a lookup until the user rules. League names and clubs come from 'sources'; the feed's own fixtures confirmed them where a match was listed.
